analysis.purpose: The Python structural parser: turns the token stream into a declaration tree (classes, functions, methods) plus a flat list of call sites, deliberately stopping short of a full expression parser because the symbol graph only needs declaration spans, nesting, and call-site heads.
responsibilities: Descend the token stream tolerantly, emitting a declaration per construct
Record nesting so members carry qualified names and member-of edges
Collect call sites in a separate whole-stream pass
Degrade on malformed input by skipping the construct rather than throwing
Drive the declaration tree from INDENT/DEDENT tokens rather than braces

businessRules.rule: Not a full expression parser — a tolerant brace/indent-level descent is enough, and is far less surface area to get wrong.
businessRules.rationale: The symbol graph needs spans, nesting and call heads; parsing expressions would add risk without adding graph value.

businessRules.rule: A malformed header degrades to skipping that logical line and never throws.
businessRules.rationale: One bad construct must not cost the whole file its symbols.

businessRules.rule: Call-site detection is a separate pass over the tokens rather than folded into the descent.
businessRules.rationale: Keeps call collection independent of how well the structural descent handled a construct.
